newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel on Thursday weakened against the dollar for the second consecutive day in mixed and volatile trading, dealers said.

"Trading opened with a sharp decline of the shekel. When the dollar reached 3.2650 it started falling because the business sector started converting dollars into shekels for end-of-the-month payments," said one dealer.
"Volume was relatively high and trading was very mixed and volatile," he added.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2570 shekels against 3.2520 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6505 shekels against 3.6509 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8663 shekels per 100 yen versus 2.8704 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.1236 shekels versus 2.1323 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2560 shekels.
